paragraphs: Ice is a floor that has not made up its mind. Yellow Duck Sweater learned this at the edge of a frozen pond, with a butter knife laced under each orange foot. A lopsided moon was sinking behind the reeds. The duck took one step, and the step kept going. Its left foot slid east, its right foot considered west, and in the ice below, another duck in a yellow sweater stood upside down, sole to sole with it. A copy, the duck thought. One of the 4,096, and skating better. Overhead a rocket climbed, chalking a white line up the clouds.

Good seed, the duck decided, and stopped arguing with its feet. It bent its knees, leaned its neck forward, and pushed. The knives hissed. The pond ran under it like a hallway with no far wall. "Wheee," it said, and the duck below said it too, in bubbles. Then came the fall, because there is always a fall: a toe caught, the sky swung, and it landed flat on its front and went on sliding on the knitted duckling. It lay with its camera eye against the ice. The duck underneath had fallen too. They rested there lens to lens, while the clouds thinned and the sun laid a single gold stripe across the pond.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The duck stands at the snowy edge of a frozen pond at dawn with a butter knife laced under each orange foot like an ice skate, under grey clouds, with a lopsided, nearly full moon sinking behind tall reeds. Panel 2: Two ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater wobbles on the grey ice with its feet sliding apart in opposite directions, and beneath the ice a second identical duck in a yellow sweater stands upside down, the soles of its feet touching the soles of the first duck's feet. Panel 3: Two ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater tilts its head down to look at the identical upside-down duck gliding smoothly beneath the ice, while high above the pond a small rocket climbs straight up and leaves a thin white trail on the grey clouds. Panel 4: The duck skates fast across the frozen pond with its knees bent and its neck leaning forward, its yellow sweater rippling in the wind and the two butter knives cutting two thin lines in the ice behind it. Panel 5: The duck trips and tips forward in mid-air just above the ice, its orange feet and butter-knife skates kicked up behind it, with the reeds and clouds tilted at an angle. Panel 6: Two ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater lies flat on its front on the ice with its round camera eye pressed to the surface, and directly beneath the ice the identical upside-down duck lies with its camera eye pressed up against the same spot, while the clouds part and one stripe of gold sunlight crosses the pond. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
